newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends listless session mixed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends listless session mixed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed Tuesday in local-dominated trading, dealers said.
Traders said activity was extremely dull, with an estimated 6,130 lots changing hands.
"Today was an inside day," said one trader. "We haven't seen any significant news and the (Brazil) weather doesn't seem to pose any threat. It seems to be a wait-and-see situation."

Benchmark September arabicas settled down 0.35 cent at 175.10 cents a lb after ranging from 179.00 to 171.75. Spot July finished 3.35 higher at 198.00, while the outer months closed up 0.20 to down 3.40.
The July/September switch widened to 22.90 cents from 19.45 cents at Monday's close.

Traders said locals spent much of the session trying to locate stops on both side of the market. An attempt to find sell stops below 170.00 cents in September was thwarted by light commission house buying, while trade selling held off a break to the upside, they said.

Technically, traders said major support for September was seen at 168.75 cents, a low reached last week. On the upside, September near-term resistance was seen at 180.00 cents, followed by 185.00 cents.

Forecasts calling for continued mild weather in top-grower Brazil has recently dampened market sentiment, traders said. No damaging cold is indicated over the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, with near to above normal temperatures, Weather Services Corp predicted Tuesday.
But while a lack of a cold threat in Brazil may limit the market's upside potential for now, traders said dwindling exchange-certified coffee stocks provided underlying support.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 250 60-kg bags as of June 23, to 46,175 bags. There were 9,512 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
